knowledge.text: Under the current diff the ordinary non-desklamp exact-target rule is stated more strictly: when the exact requested noun phrase has not been observed, do not acquire, clean, cool, heat, or place a different but related object, and leave a container that holds only a non-matching object. This was not reliably followed in the current clean-butterknife-and-put-it-in-drawer pair: the exact butterknife was never observed, drawer 1 held a knife 1 and a spatula 1 (P7:2, Q7:4), and both sides manipulated the near-miss knife — the Parent took it (P7:8) and the Candidate took it (Q7:9), then cleaned it (Q7:17) and moved it (Q7:19) — with both reaching the 50-step limit. In the paired put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet task the exact soapbar was likewise absent and the nearest visible objects were candle 2, soapbottle 2 and spraybottle 2 in cabinet 2 (P8:6, Q8:7); there neither side picked up a near-miss, yet both also hit the 50-step limit. So the strengthened exact-noun-phrase wording neither reliably prevented near-miss manipulation (one clear violation) nor converted an absent-target failure into success, narrowing the earlier reading that the Candidate reliably abstains from near-miss objects.

The stricter no-substitute wording coexisted with preserved exact-target acquisition and placement when the requested object was actually reachable: in the put-some-pencil-on-desk pair both sides opened drawer 1, saw pencil 1 next to a non-matching creditcard 2, took only the pencil (P5:3, Q5:4) and placed it on desk 1; in both mug-to-sidetable pairs both sides took mug 1 from diningtable 1 and moved it to sidetable 1 (P3:2, Q3:2, P4:2, Q4:2); and in the put-a-clean-butterknife-in-drawer pair both sides took butterknife 1 from countertop 2 (P6:3, Q6:3), cleaned it and placed it in drawer 1. These pairs are among the eight current pairs in which both sides succeeded, so no degradation of ordinary exact-target retrieval was observed.

Earlier incarnations of the same no-substitute principle (inside the temperature-conditioned placement guidance of the two prior edits) were examined when the exact target was absent: in a cool-a-pan task the Parent eventually took and cooled a pot while the Candidate repeatedly saw the pot without taking or moving it; in a heat-a-mug task the Parent took and heated a cup while the Candidate left the visible cup untouched; and in a hot-mug placement task the Parent took cup 2 from the countertop and heated it while the Candidate left the visible cup untouched. All these executions still reached the step limit because the exact pan or mug was not found, so abstention saved substitution steps but produced no success. This preserves the conditional-usefulness limit: the rule can avoid ineffective near-miss manipulation, but its task-level value depends on the exact target existing in an inspectable location, and the current stronger wording does not guarantee adherence either.

The current diff rewrote the ordinary non-desklamp search step to include visible open surfaces (tables, countertops, shelves, sidetables) rather than only closed drawers/cabinets, to leave an opened receptacle that lacks the target and pick a different uninspected candidate from the current admissible list, not to re-enter a location just left or repeat a short cycle, and to prefer a receptacle type not yet tried. The response is mixed. In the clean-butterknife pair both sides cycled among drawers 1–7 (the Candidate returned to drawer 1 at Q7:12 and Q7:30 and then traversed drawers 1–5 again at Q7:45–Q7:49) and hit the 50-step limit without finding a butterknife. In the put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet pair both sides cycled among cabinets 1–4, with the Candidate adding two receptacle types the Parent never visited — bathtubbasin 1 (Q8:3) and sinkbasin 2 (Q8:19, Q8:43, Q8:49) — and still hitting the limit. So the broader-surface/no-revisit/prefer-new-type wording was followed only in isolated instances and did not break the cycling/step-limit failure mode when the exact target was absent.

The prior round's search rewrite had added: use current and recent observations to avoid immediate cycling; do not re-examine an already-open empty receptacle or check inventory while carrying nothing; and, when the obvious cabinets/fridge have not yielded the target or the step count is already high, prefer uninspected drawers, shelves, the diningtable, or other listed receptacles and new unopened containers over known-empty locations. Its observed response was mixed: in one cool-a-bread instance the Parent cycled among the fridge, cabinets and countertops and hit the step limit without finding bread, whereas the Candidate expanded to the diningtable, took a bread there, cooled it at the fridge and placed it on countertop 1, succeeding; but in another cool-a-bread pair with an identical room and contents the Parent explored countertop 3 and took the bread there while the Candidate never went to countertop 3 and cycled among cabinets, shelves and the fridge to the limit, and in a cool-a-plate pair the Candidate reached the plate in cabinet 9 only at step 49 and exhausted the budget one step later while the Parent finished at step 38. Across that round the net task-level result was slightly lower for the Candidate (6 successes vs 7), within plausible stochastic variation. Thus the anti-cycling/step-budget language was already unreliably followed, with failures concentrated when the exact target was absent.

The current diff added a distinct Admissible Actions section requiring the Actor to verify that a navigation or manipulation command is present in the current admissible-action list before issuing it, and, when a desired navigation destination is absent but a direct action on that receptacle is listed, to use the direct action or otherwise choose a listed action that advances the task. The verify-before-issuing behavior was not reliably followed: in the put-a-clean-soapbar-in-cabinet pair the Candidate issued 'go to cabinet 3' from cabinet 1 although it was not admissible, producing 'Nothing happens' with action_in_admissible_commands=false (Q8:39), then examined that same already-open location (Q8:40); the no-clause Parent in the same pair likewise produced inadmissible steps (an empty action at P8:12 and an unavailable 'go to cabinet 1' at P8:15). In every other current Candidate pair (the eight successes) all actions were admissible, so no positive application of the fallback branch was observed, and no current task displayed a desired-but-unavailable navigation destination being replaced by a listed direct action. Thus the evidence supports only limited adherence: one observed violation, with the substitute-direct-action branch untested.
